text.title: django-decision-tree Decision Tree
text.summary: The architecture decision tree itself: framework → API → layering → DB → deployment, plus the per-unit code-placement branch used after the tier is chosen.

decision-tree.root-question: Score on five Django-fit signals (admin / ORM / SSR / accounts / forms): how many apply?

branch.question: DRF or Ninja or vanilla Django views?

branch.conclusion: framework="fastapi" (API-only) or "flask" (lightweight). Skip the rest of the Django tree.
Consider "django-ninja-only" — Django ORM + admin but Ninja for the API layer.

branch.question: Model count + team size + bounded contexts?
What does this unit of code actually do?

branch.conclusion: layer="views". One service call, ≤ 25 lines, no ORM.
layer="utils". stdlib imports only; tests assert f(x) == y with no mocks.
layer="tasks". One service call and a return, nothing else.
layer="integrations". Primitives across the boundary; no domain models.

text.example: signals: {needs_admin=true, needs_orm=true, needs_ssr=false, needs_accounts=true, needs_forms=true} → score=4 q-framework -> >= 4 (django) q-api -> 'existing-drf-or-complex-perms' (team familiar) => api_stack=drf models=12 → '10-50 models' => layering=service-layer

unit = "charge the customer's card and record the payment" scope -> place-one-unit-of-code q-placement -> writes-db-or-calls-an-external-system => layer=services, @transaction.atomic, Stripe call delegated to integrations/stripe.py taking primitives (r8, r12)
